sentences.text: In this petition, the land of the petitioner has been acquired for widening of the road in National Highway No. 12(A) from Chilphi to Simga Section in District Kabirdham.

The award was passed on 05.02.2016 in which the compensation awarded to the petitioner for entire land is Rs.
1,92,84,430/-, however, respondent No. 4 has paid Rs. 1,54,64, 422/- only to the petitioner and the difference amount of compensation Rs. 43,20,008/- has not been paid to him.
Against the illegal action of respondent No.4, the petitioner preferred a representation before respondent No.4 on 09.01.2017 but the same was not decided by him.

2. Record of the case would show that the petitioner was the owner of the land situated at P.H. No.
22, R.I. Circle-Bodla, Tahsil Bodla, District Kabirdham having khasra No. (143/2, 279,304)6,

sentences.text: Notification of under Section 3A of National Highways Act was issued by the Central Government and after calling of the objection notification under Section 3D was issued and thereafter Land Acquisition Officer/ Sub Divisonal Officer (Revenue) Kabhirdham who was appointed as Land Acquisition Officer passed the award on 05.02.2003 and determined the compensation to the tune of Rs. 1,92,84,430/- but Rs. 1,54,64, 422/- has been paid.

4. Counsel for the petitioner would submit that the heads in which the compensation has been determined have also been mentioned in Annexure P/2, wherein they have taken care of every thing attached with the property including trees planted in the land.

He would further submit that after passing of award, Sub-Divisional Officer (Revenue) has moved an application on 22.07.2016 before the Collector for review of the order and the Collector has granted permission for review on 26.07.2016 thereafter the same was reviewed and as per review order dated 03.08.2016, Rs.
43,20,008/- was reduced from the compensation awarded to the petitioner.

He would further submit that the procedure adopted by the Land Acquisition Officer is nonest, without jurisdiction and illegal, therefore, he would submit that reduction of quantum be kindly set aside and the respondents be directed to make payment of Rs. 43,20,008/- towards additional compensation along with the interest.

5. On the other hand, State counsel would submit that review application was filed and there was some arithmetic mistake apparent on the face of record, therefore, the mistake has been considered and the Court has rightly passed the award reducing the compensation.
6. Counsel for the respondent No.1 would submit that the procedure adopted by Sub-Divisional Officer (Revenue) is contrary to the provisions contained in National Highways Act.

He would further submit that the National Highways Act is a complete code which provides how the compensation has to be determined for construction of National Highways and Section 3G(5) also provides the determination of amount payable as compensation.
Section 3G(5) is reproduced below:-
Section

3G(5 ) if the amount determined by the competent authority under sub section (1) or sub-section (2) is not acceptable to either of the parties, the amount shall, on an application by either of the parties, be determined by the arbitrator to be appointed by the Central Government and Arbitrator has been appointed in this regard.
7. From the record, it is quite vivid that the application for review of award was not moved by respondent No. 2 National Highway Authority of India.

The application for review was moved by Land Acquisition Officer who has no authority to move an application for review or recall its own order after passing of the order as he becomes functions officio after passing of the award.

The land acqusition proceedings was initiated for construction of National Highways, therefore, it has to be governed and controlled by the provisions of National Highways Act, 1956 any divergent from the procedure prescribed under the Act will nullify the whole action.

sentences.text: Considering this aspect of the matter, also considering National Highways Act, 1956 which is complete code and also considering Section 3G(5) which provides for mechanism and further considering the legal position that the Sub- Divisional Officer (Revenue) has no power to reduce the quantum it is held that the award dated 03.8.2016 reducing the compensation is bad in law as such same is liable to be quashed and accordingly it is quashed.
9. However, liberty is granted to National Highways to move an application if so advised, before the Arbitrator.
If they are not satisfied with the award as per Section 3G of the National Highways Act.

It is made clear that in the eventuality of filing of application by the authority before the Arbitrator, the Arbitrator shall issue notice to the present petitioner thereafter he will decide the issue in accordance with the law considering the provisions of National Highways Act, 1956.
10. With the aforesaid observation, the writ petition is disposed of.
